title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection of latency/throughput regressions and add rollout guards
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: our continuous performance canary sometimes misses short-lived but high-impact latency/throughput regressions during rollouts because it uses a fixed-window baseline and simple percent-delta checks. This PR enhances the canary detector with robust statistical detection, dynamic baselines, and automated rollout guard actions. Motivation: reduce customer-facing latency regressions caused by rollout changes and provide automated, service-level rollout protections that can be enabled per-route or globally. Changes in this PR: 1) New detection algorithm: z-score / EWMA hybrid to detect both step and gradual regressions with configurable sensitivity and signal smoothing. 2) Dynamic baseline windows: baseline selection prefers recent stable periods but falls back to long-term baseline when traffic is low. 3) Multi-metric detection: simultaneous checks for p50/p95 latency and throughput drop with configurable gating rules. 4) Rollout guard actions: automatic pause/rollback triggers available in rollout policy; guard reasons recorded as structured events in observability. 5) Integration with canary lab and optimizer so the detector can be tested in simulation before enabling. 6) New end-to-end perf tests and unit coverage for detector edge cases. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear: ENG-4721) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf tests in perf-canary harness - [x] metrics/trace additions and dashboards - [x] feature-flag behind `canary_auto_detect_v2` How to test: run perf-canary harness against a patched redwood-serving image; there are synthetic regressions in perf-canary/testdata that exercise step, ramp, and noise patterns. The canary runner exposes a simulation flag that exercises the rollback path. Observability: added metrics canary.detector.zscore, canary.detector.sensitivity, canary.rollout.guard.count and tracing spans around DetectRegression. Migration and rollout: feature behind a feature-flag; default behavior unchanged. Ops can enable per-customer routes via rollout policy in Console. Related: SRE-198 (alert tuning), ENG-4721 (design), see notes in the PR.
